layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Tubular structure segmentation (TSS) is important for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various applications, such as hemodynamic analysis and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: route navigation. Despite significant progress in TSS, do-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: main shifts remain a major challenge, leading to per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formance degradation in unseen target domains. Un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: like other segmentation tasks, TSS is more sensitive to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain shifts, as changes in topological structures can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compromise segmentation integrity, and variations in lo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cal features distinguishing foreground from background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., texture and contrast) may further disrupt topologi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cal continuity. To address these challenges, we propose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Topology-enhanced Test-Time Adaptation (TopoTTA), the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: first test-time adaptation framework designed specifically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for TSS. TopoTTA consists of two stages: Stage 1 adapts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models to cross-domain topological discrepancies using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the proposed Topological Meta Difference Convolutions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (TopoMDCs), which enhance topological representation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without altering pre-trained parameters; Stage 2 improves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topological continuity by a novel Topology Hard sample

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Generation (TopoHG) strategy and prediction alignment on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hard samples with pseudo-labels in the generated pseudo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: breaks. Extensive experiments across four scenarios and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ten datasets demonstrate TopoTTA's effectiveness in han-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dling topological distribution shifts, achieving an average

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvement of 31.81% in clDice. TopoTTA also serves as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a plug-and-play TTA solution for CNN-based TSS models.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Tubular structure segmentation (TSS), also known as curvi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: linear object segmentation [45], plays a critical role in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various applications (e.g., hemodynamic analysis [24, 55]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and route planning [64, 73]). Although many TSS meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods have been proposed and achieved inspiring perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance [15, 21], domain shifts remain a common challenge

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in real-world scenarios [42] due to discrepancies in imaging

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: devices [1, 13] and sample heterogeneity [11].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Domain shifts undermine the effectiveness of TSS mod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: els trained on the source domain when applied to an un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seen target domain [36, 50]. Unlike segmentation models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained for other tasks, e.g., semantic [35, 67] or tumor seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation [9, 30, 31, 47, 77], TSS models are more sensi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tive to domain shifts [50]. Beyond the common variations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such as contrast and noise distribution [62, 63], TSS faces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: additional challenges related to unseen topological struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tural characteristics, including variations in trajectory, cur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vature, branching patterns, and thickness [6, 46]. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: factors degrade segmentation performance and even dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rupt the topological continuity of the structures [65] (see

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1 (b1)), which may mislead critical downstream appli-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *Corresponding authors.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recently, a special domain adaptation (DA) paradigm,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: namely test-time adaptation (TTA) [27, 40, 43], has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed and successfully applied to various image seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation tasks, including semantic [22, 60, 61] and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image segmentation [3, 74]. Unlike other DA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paradigms, TTA performs continuous online adaptation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: during the test stage (after model deployment) [71]. It uses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extremely small amounts of data (e.g., a single sample or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: batch), aligning better with real-world scenarios where data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: must be processed sequentially [58].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Most TTA methods update pre-trained models using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: self-supervised methods [27], which can typically be cat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: egorized into normalization-based methods [58, 72] and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teacher-student schemes [10, 60]. Normalization-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods update normalization layer statistics [53] (e.g.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: batch/layer normalization (BN/LN)) or leverage the differ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ence in normalization statistics before and after adaptation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to update external model parameters [3, 49]. These meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods are initially designed for classification tasks, and their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance may degrade when applied to segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks with severe pixel-level class imbalance [5]. The sec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ond category, teacher-student schemes (based on pseudo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labels), updates all model parameters and achieves perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance gains in general segmentation tasks [69]. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as shown in Fig. 1, these methods perform poorly in TSS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: due to two unique challenges in cross-domain scenarios:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Challenge 1: Discrepant topological structures. Tubu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lar structures in the source and target domains can ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hibit substantial topological differences (e.g., thickness,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curvature, and branching patterns). Prior TTA methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: general-purpose model adaptation strategies struggle to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectively capture these cross-domain topological varia-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions when adapting to individual samples.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Challenge 2: Fragile topological continuity. In cross-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain settings, the local characteristics (e.g., color, tex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture, and contrast) distinguishing foreground from back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground may change significantly [50]. Existing TTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods lack targeted adaptation to these local variations,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resulting in catastrophic disruptions to topological conti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nuity (see Fig. 1) by misclassifying foreground pixels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To address the aforementioned challenges, we propose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Topology-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation (TopoTTA) in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this paper. It includes two adaptation stages: topological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure adaptation (Stage 1) and topological continuity re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: finement (Stage 2).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Stage 1 aims to enhance the model's capability to adapt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to discrepant topological structures by utilizing a topology-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perceiving model adaptation strategy. Inspired by the Cen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tral Difference Convolution (CDC) [70], which captures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differences between the central pixel and its neighbors to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhance local representations, we extend this concept to ac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: commodate the elongated and diverse trajectories of tubu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lar structures. Specifically, we introduce Topological Meta

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Difference Convolutions (TopoMDCs), which perform a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dual-pixel difference operation by extending the central

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel's interaction across eight directional neighbors. As

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Fig. 2, we learn weighted combinations of differ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ent directional TopoMDCs (instead of the vanilla convolu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion) for different regions to enhance the representations of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hard-to-detect tubular branches, improving adaptability to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: discrepant topological structures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Within Stage 2, we design a Topology Hard sample

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Generation (TopoHG) strategy to construct samples with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pseudo-breaks. These pseudo-breaks mislead the models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to make weakened predictions with poor topological conti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nuity. We then emphasize the local consistency between the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predictions and original pseudo-labels in these hard regions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This stage encourages the models to adapt the characteris-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tics distinguishing foreground from background and helps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: address continuity destructions in the target domain.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our contributions are as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We propose the first TTA framework for tubular structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation, named TopoTTA, which effectively adapts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to unseen domains by enhancing topological information.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We design eight directional Topological Meta Difference

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Convolutions (TopoMDCs) within TopoTTA, and learn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: how to adaptively combine different TopoMDCs based on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the topological features of the test sample. TopoMDCs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhance adaptability to unseen topological structures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We propose a Topology Hard sample Generation strategy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for TopoTTA, namely TopoHG, which generates pseudo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: breaks at confidently predicted regions. We then align

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the predictions around these pseudo breaks to the original

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pseudo labels, improving the topological continuity in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unseen domain.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Extensive experiments on four scenarios across ten

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets validate the effectiveness of TopoTTA in address-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing topological distribution shifts, achieving an average

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance improvement of 31.81% in clDice.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Related Works

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1. Tubular Structure Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Tubular structures, characterized by their thin and long

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topological structures as well as complex layouts, usually

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cannot be accurately and continuously localized by general

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation methods [59]. To tackle these challenges, re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: searchers have incorporated topological priors into model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: designs, including specialized deformable convolution ker-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nels [46], attention mechanisms [14, 66], and tailored model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: architectures [33]. Complementary to these module inno-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vations, PointScatter [59] was introduced to represent tubu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lar structures as point sets, addressing the flexibility limita-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions of masks constrained by fixed grids. DconnNet [68]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: employed a unique design to separate directional subspaces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the latent space, enhancing feature representation for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.2. Test-Time Adaptation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: TTA adaptively adjusts the model at test time based on a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: small number of unlabeled samples from a different distri-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bution. Early TTA methods primarily modified model rep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resentations by adjusting BN's statistics [38, 44, 61, 75].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mirza et al. [38] adapted target domain features by updat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing BN statistics continuously. Most TTA methods used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: self-supervised learning to adjust pre-trained parameters,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including normalization-based methods [3, 43, 53, 58, 72]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and teacher-student (TS) schemes [10, 41, 56, 60]. Wang

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. [58] proposed TENT, an entropy minimization method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that updates BN affine transformation parameters to im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prove confidence in the target domain. Motivated by TENT,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some recent works achieved better performance [3, 72] by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: designing various strategies to fine-tune BN. Zhang et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [72] incorporated source domain statistics and extended the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entropy minimization loss to utilize target domain informa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion better. More recently, Chen et al. [3] reduced general-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ization errors by aligning source and target statistics to up-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: date external model parameters. However, many TTA meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods are designed for classification tasks, ignoring pixel-wise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: class imbalance. In segmentation tasks, where sample im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: balance is more severe, simple statistical adjustments and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: minor parameter updates are easily dominated by the ma-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jority of background pixels, reducing segmentation perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance [69]. The TS scheme, which applies consistency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: regularization to update all model parameters, has shown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectiveness in general segmentation tasks. CoTTA [60]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used weight-averaged and augmentation-averaged predic-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions, further reducing error accumulation in continuous in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ference. However, these methods lack a focus on tubular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure and topological continuity, leading to performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decline and continuity destruction in TSS.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Proposed TopoTTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1. Preliminary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Let

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denote the labeled source domain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 4.1. Experiment Setup

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Datasets. We adopt 10 widely-used TSS datasets for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the following experiments. The retinal vessel seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation datasets are collected from three different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sources: DRIVE [54], STARE [16], and CHASEDB1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (CHASE) [12], which contain 40, 20, and 28 samples,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: respectively. Three road extraction datasets are Deep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Globe [8], Massachusetts road (MR) [39], and CNDS [4],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: providing 8,570, 1,171, and 224 samples, respectively. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: microscopic neuronal segmentation datasets are Neub1 and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Neub2 [76], with 112 and 98 samples, respectively. Two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinal OCT-angiography vessel segmentation datasets are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from different sources, ROSE1 [37] and OCTA500 [26],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing 117 and 300 samples, respectively. All datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: follow their original training and testing splits, except for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: STARE, which is officially used as a test set due to its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limited sample size [16].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Evaluation Metrics. Following prior works [46, 59, 65,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 68], we use Dice as the primary metric for TSS perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance evaluation, with clDice [52] and Betti errors (β) [18]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as metrics of topological continuity. In Table 1, the diag-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: onal marks “" in clDice for some TTA methods indicate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cases where no skeleton map can be extracted from their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predictions, and thus clDice cannot be calculated. Further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: investigation reveals that these are failure cases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model pre-trained on a single dataset (source domain) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test it on other datasets (target domains) to calculate met-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rics. UNet [48] and CS2Net [24] (designed for TSS) are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adopted as baseline networks for validating the performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of TopoTTA. To ensure consistent field-of-view and cross-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain accuracy, all datasets are resized to 384 × 384 pix-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: els, except for the OCTA dataset as ROSE and OCTA500

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: already share similar resolutions. During testing, TopoTTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the comparison methods undergo six iterations of adap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation for each image, with TopoTTA performing three iter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Comparison TTA Methods. In the following experiments,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we compare our method with three categories of TTA meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods: (1) methods designed for semantic segmentation, such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as CoTTA [60] and DIGA [61], (2) a method designed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: works as TopoTTA, using hyperparameters as specified in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the corresponding reference or assigning optimal ones.

layout_dets.text: 5. Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this work, we proposed the first TTA framework, i.e.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topological continuity. To improve the adaptability to topo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adaptively integrate various orientation information accord-

layout_dets.text: ing to the topological feature of each test sample. Besides,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hance the predictions' topological continuity. Extensive ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: periments across four scenarios verified the superiority of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our TopoTTA compared to other methods.
